name: Anfiteatro de Mérida

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/1316311 (centre of the ellipses fitted to the outer way 89067879 and to the arena walls, ways 89067885, 1206491700 and 1206491716; long axis at 134–137°, the main gate at its north-west end)

rights.note: Roman amphitheatre inaugurated in 8 BC (inscriptions of the tribunes), planned together with the theatre beside it; architects unknown. Excavated from 1919; the lower seats were partly rebuilt by José Menéndez-Pidal in the mid 20th century. Part of the Archaeological Ensemble of Mérida (UNESCO World Heritage).

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q2360379_anfiteatro_de_merida.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. The amphitheatre as it stands today: the sanded arena with its podium wall; the cross-shaped fossa in the middle, its central basin and short south-west arm open, the long arms under the present wooden decks; the ima cavea (nine rows) rebuilt by the gates and the tribunes and rough elsewhere, the praecinctio and the balteus; the two tribunes on the minor axis (the editor's on the east with its two stairs, the west one over the passage to the outside); the two long galleries on the long axis, open to the sky with brick transverse arches, and the low walls of the rooms beside them; the lost media and summa cavea as a grassy slope of rubble crossed by the radial walls of the fourteen other passages, higher on the east, where the cavea leans on the hill of San Albín; the outer wall standing only in parts. Simplified or uncertain: the rows are drawn as offset curves of the outer ellipse (published sizes, not a survey); which stretches of the outer wall stand and how high (approximate, from the orthophoto and photos); the inner vaults, rooms and stairs (not modelled); the depth of the fossa (about 2.8 m).
